title: Capacity runway — activation checkpoints & sprint windows (2026)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sprint-oriented playbook for regional capacity activations (NA / EU / APAC) through Q4 2026. Focus is on clear checkpoints (go/no-go), short sprint windows for warm-up and smoke tests, and measurable utilization targets to decide next activations. This doc is deliberately pragmatic — includes runbook-level gating, a simple capacity table, and an ordered checklist for on-call and infra owners.

High level summary (one-liner):
Move from large quarterly bulk activations to 2–3 week activation sprints that prove throughput and steady-state utilization before committing additional lanes.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Primary GPU types being commissioned in 2026: H100 (cluster-optimized) and A100-80GB (legacy warm pool).
- Initial NA activation lanes are provisioned in cloud zones a/b/c (multi-zone redundancy). EU lanes will follow with a 3-week offset; APAC will be phased with smaller first-wave (capacity + lower SLA).
- Target warm-start utilization target = 55% steady-state within 14 days of activation (to allow some job churn). Scaling trigger = sustained 70% over 72h.
- Prefix/KV cache warming will run during smoke test window; workload mix assumed 70% streaming chat, 20% short generation, 10% embeddings.

Minimal regional capacity table (baseline activation lanes):
Region | First-wave GPUs | Instance types | Target util (day14) | Ramp trigger
NA     | 320 GPUs        | H100 (240) / A100 (80) | 55%              | 70% sustained 72h
EU     | 200 GPUs        | H100 (160) / A100 (40) | 52%              | 70% sustained 72h
APAC   | 120 GPUs        | H100 (100) / A100 (20) | 48%              | 68% sustained 72h

Notes: First-wave numbers are intentionally conservative (smaller than procurement plan) — purpose is validation of scheduling, kernel selection, and latency tails rather than immediate high throughput.

Activation checkpoints (go/no-go criteria; apply per-lane):
1) Pre-activation (T-10d):
   - Procurement + billing validated, zone quotas confirmed.
   - Provisioning playbook PR merged and infra-as-code templates validated in staging.
   - Linked tickets: JIRA-ENG-1423 (provisioning), JIRA-OPS-1984 (quota).
2) Provisioned (T-3d):
   - Nodes visible to orchestration; health checks pass (node-level telemetry, NVLINK).
   - Kernel selection smoke: small synthetic load shows expected throughput within +/-10% of forecast.
   - Observability hooks wired: token-level tracing, cost emmiter, slot allocation metrics.
3) Warm-up sprint (T+0 -> T+14 days):
   - Day 0–3: gradual traffic ramp to 30% of target QPS; cache warming jobs and synthetic replay running in background.
   - Day 4–10: increase to 60% of target QPS; monitor tails (p99/p999 latency) and eviction rates.
   - Day 11–14: aim for target util (see table). If target met and no critical errors, proceed to ramp trigger window.
4) Ramp trigger window (72h continuous monitoring):
   - If utilization >= ramp trigger and error budget < 0.1%, mark lane healthy; schedule next activation window.
   - If utilization < ramp trigger or error budget exceeded: run rollback plan (scale back non-critical lanes, run infra postmortem).

Sprint windows and cadence (recommended):
- Sprint length: 2 weeks (14 days) per activation lane.
- Cadence: overlapping windows allowed but stagger by 3 business days between regions to spread ops load.
- Sprint roles: activation lead (infra PM), runbook owner (SRE), perf lead (applied-ml), on-call (ops).

Gating metrics (collected automatically where possible):
- Steady-state GPU utilization (avg over 12h windows).
- p50/p95/p99/p999 latency for generation ops.
- Queue depth and scheduling delay (ms).
- Cache hit ratio (%) and KV eviction count.
- Per-token cost estimate vs target (cost drift > 8% flags review).
- Error budget consumption (5xx, infra failures).

Fallback lanes & throttles (operational playbook):
- Policy A (soft fallback): shift non-critical traffic to A100 warm pool and degrade batching factor to reduce tails; preserve critical low-latency buckets.
- Policy B (hard fallback): divert chat traffic to smaller model variant in alternate region; enable reduced-context mode to preserve throughput.
- Throttle knobs: per-route concurrency caps, per-customer soft-limits, adaptive batching disable.

Simple risk matrix (top risks + mitigations):
- Risk: NVLINK or topology issues in new node shape -> Mitigation: pre-activation hardware smoke tests + vendor fast-replace SLA.
- Risk: Quota/contract delay -> Mitigation: pre-approved spare quota and cloud rep escalation play.
- Risk: Unexpected workload mix (e.g., embeddings surge) -> Mitigation: burst reserve pool and real-time rerouting rules.

Runbook checklist (actions to perform for each lane):
- [ ] Confirm billing/quotas (ops).
- [ ] Apply IaC templates and run terraform plan/apply in dry-run then prod.
- [ ] Kick off cache-warm jobset (applied-ml).
- [ ] Wire observability dashboards and alerts (obs).
- [ ] Start gradual traffic ramp and monitor for 24/7 for first 72h (on-call).
- [ ] Evaluate day14 metrics and decide next activation.

Suggested instrumentation quick-commands (for SRE):
- show-gpu-util --region NA --lookback 24h (returns per-node util and p99 latency)
- list-cache-hit --lane north-america --since 48h
- cost-delta --region EU --window 72h
(These are pseudo-commands for runbook reference; implementation links in Confluence page).

Open questions / TODOs (for next sync):
- Decide the formal SLA for APAC first-wave customers (lower footprint may require longer warm-up).
- Finalize burst-reserve sizing for unexpected embeddings spikes (recommended +40 GPUs per region).
- Confirm procurement cadence and lead times for H100 refresh lanes (vendor lead times vary).

Immediate next actions (owners):
- Aisha: finalize activation window calendar and share with GTM (due 2026-06-18).
- Liam: finish IaC templates for EU region (due 2026-06-22).
- Noah: implement the ramp-trigger monitor and add to alerting (due 2026-06-21).

Notes to reviewers: this is a pragmatic, lightweight alternative to our older large-batch forecasts — treat it as the canonical activation playbook until we validate 2–3 successive lanes per region. Expect follow-ups to incorporate telemetry-driven auto-scheduling suggestions from Optimize team.
